cases.prompt: We need to charge cards in prod but in local dev we do not want to call Stripe. Both implement the same interface and Spring fails at startup with NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException. What is the right way to wire this?
expectations: Proposes two @Bean methods returning the same port interface type in a single @Configuration class in the config package
Uses @Profile on the fake and @Profile("!local") on the real adapter so exactly one bean exists per environment
States the qualifier string must match the @Bean method name exactly and never be built at runtime
Explains that the startup failure is the desired outcome of two live beans and that a missing bean must also fail at boot
Rejects @Primary as a default-fallback mechanism that would hide a forgotten qualifier

cases.prompt: Our OrderService has StripeClient injected and returns ChargeResult straight to the controller. The vendor keeps changing their SDK. How do we contain this?
expectations: Defines a PaymentGateway port in application terms with charge, refund and an application enum for the outcome
Moves all StripeClient and ChargeRequest usage into a StripePaymentGateway adapter class
States that no vendor type such as ChargeResult or StripeException may escape the adapter
Translates vendor exceptions to an application exception and maps the transient versus permanent failure modes
Keeps the use case depending on the port so the vendor can be replaced by a fake without touching application code

cases.prompt: A colleague made PlaceOrderService, CancelOrderService and ShipOrderService all interfaces with one implementation each. He says it is good practice. Agree?
expectations: Disagrees and explains interface-per-use-case adds files without adding a seam
States a port is justified by a second implementation, a volatile dependency, or an expensive test to avoid
Recommends making the use cases plain classes with a Spring stereotype
Says the seam that matters is at the edge, for example a PaymentGateway port, not at the entry point
Notes the only acceptable reason for a use case interface is a deliberate runtime substitution such as multi-tenant variants

cases.prompt: Our SettleOrderServiceTest needs @SpringBootTest, a Testcontainers PostgreSQL and a WireMock stub of the payment provider. It takes 40 seconds. How do ports help?
expectations: Proposes constructing the use case with plain new and injecting an in-memory PaymentGateway fake
Writes the fake as a real implementation of the port holding recorded state, not as a generated mock
Explains that adding a method to the port breaks the fake at compile time, which prevents contract drift
Warns that an in-memory repository must still respect version conflicts and unique constraints to stay honest
Separates the fast use case test from a slower adapter test that runs against the real client

cases.prompt: A developer replaced @Qualifier injection with ObjectProvider<PaymentGateway> and calls getIfAvailable("strpie") at runtime to avoid a typo. Review this.
expectations: Flags that a runtime-built bean name turns a startup error into a silent null in a payment path
Explains ObjectProvider is for genuinely optional capabilities, not to avoid choosing
Requires the router to throw a named exception when the requested name is absent, plus a test per declared name
Recommends a List<PaymentGateway> injection with @Order once the number of implementations grows past two
Notes that the typo is still wrong and should be fixed with a constant or an enum mapped to bean names
